text:
Ava (support): Hey team, hitting an odd one from customer AcmeApp — after a forced password reset via their IdP (Okta) a subset of users keep getting repeated MFA prompts in our embedded widget while other endpoints show them as logged in. They see the SSO flow succeed but the app asks for MFA again on any new request.

Samir (eng): Do we have a repro? sounds like a session mismatch between our session cookie and the new IdP assertion. Could be a cookie domain/scoping issue or two different session stores.

Ava (support): I got steps from the customer. Repro (high-level):
1) User on chrome-login.example.com -> signs in at idp.acme.com (Okta) -> resets password via IdP UI.
2) IdP issues new SAML/OIDC assertion and redirects back to our app.
3) Embedded SDK receives 200 and sets Authorization: Bearer <new-id-token>. IdP shows active session.
4) Immediately any subsequent API call (graphQL /v1/chat) returns 401 prompting MFA/UI to re-run login.

They supplied a packet capture and a browser console log. Notably the response headers from our auth endpoint show a Set-Cookie for session with domain=app.example.com, SameSite=Lax. The embedded widget runs on chrome-login.example.com (different subdomain).

Tara - SRE: That smells like a cross-subdomain cookie visibility problem. SameSite=Lax can block cookies on cross-site POSTs/back-channel flows, and domain=app.example.com won't be sent by chrome-login.example.com. But why did some endpoints work?

Liam (infra): Two possible vectors: (A) The widget uses the id token for frontend auth but our backend routes still check for our session cookie; if the cookie isn't sent the backend rejects. (B) We have a stale session binding / device trust token stored in the other cookie (device_jwt) that doesn't get rotated on password reset and fails device trust checks.

Jules (support): Customer mentioned this only started after an IdP-initiated password reset flow last week (rolled to production on 2026-02-25). Before that everything was fine.

InfraBot: Incident note: rolling deploy of session-service v2.4.1 started 2026-03-02 02:15 UTC. Could be related to cookie attribute change.

Samir (eng): Can you paste the relevant headers/snippets? Also need their SDK config (cookieDomain, sameSite) and whether they're using embedded vs redirect flows.

Ava (support): Paste from customer packet: 
```
Request: POST https://auth.example.com/session/refresh
Response 302 -> https://chrome-login.example.com/return
Set-Cookie: _rwd_session=eyJ..; Domain=app.example.com; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=2592000
Set-Cookie: device_jwt=eyJ..; Domain=chrome-login.example.com; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Max-Age=604800
```
And their widget does an XHR POST to /v1/auth/handshake (from chrome-login.example.com) immediately after. The browser does not send _rwd_session with that request.

Tara - SRE: Yeah that explains it — our session cookie scoped to app.example.com won't be attached from chrome-login.example.com. We likely used to set Domain=.example.com previously. Did we change that in the deploy InfraBot called out?

Liam (infra): Checking changelog... session-service 2.4.1 introduced stricter cookie scoping for SSO hardening. The intention was to prevent cookie leakage to shared subdomains, but this regressed the embedded-widget flow for customers hosting the widget on a sibling subdomain.

Samir (eng): Two-part remediation: short-term instruct customer to host widget on app.example.com or configure widget to use redirect flow (server-side handshake), or we can flip a temporary toggle to set Domain=.example.com and SameSite=None for cross-subdomain flows. Long-term we should detect embedded handoffs and use a cross-domain handshake using the OIDC code flow + backend cookie set on return domain.

Jules (support): Customer asked for a timeline. Can we get a quick mitigation (toggle) and a safe rollback plan? They have 200 seats affected.

Tara - SRE: We can enable a feature-flag on the session-service to restore legacy Domain=.example.com and SameSite=None for a subset of tenants while we build a proper fix. However we need to check CSRF protections and audit logs — making cookies cross-site increases risk.

Samir (eng): Agreed. Add these acceptance tests before flipping: 
- Ensure we set Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None and Domain=.example.com only when tenant allows embedded widget API.
- Validate device_jwt binding rotation on password reset: when IdP signals password change, invalidate device_jwt and force device rebind.
- Add an automated regression that mimics the chrome-login.example.com -> app.example.com flow (integration test with real cookie behavior).

Ava (support): I ran a quick curl repro from customer (they gave this):
```bash
# simulate IdP redirect response to our handshake endpoint
curl -v -X GET 'https://auth.example.com/handshake?code=abc' -H 'Host: chrome-login.example.com' -c cookies.txt -L
# then immediate API call that should include _rwd_session but doesn't
curl -v -X POST 'https://api.example.com/v1/chat' -b cookies.txt -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"input":"test"}'
```
The first curl ends with Set-Cookie for _rwd_session (domain=app.example.com) and cookies.txt doesn't attach it on the second call.

Liam (infra): Good repro. For the mitigation toggle we need: feature-flag + firewall rule to limit to tenant AcmeApp until we get approval from security. I'll own the rollout if Eng signs off.

Samir (eng): I'll implement the toggle and the device_jwt invalidation in session-service. ETA for patch and canary: 6 hours. Once deployed, Tara can schedule controlled rollouts.

Tara - SRE: I'll prepare canaries (10 users) and monitor login latencies + auth 5xx/401 metrics. Also watch for CSRF spikes.

Jules (support): I'll tell AcmeApp: short-term workaround—use redirect flow or host the widget on app.example.com; we can also enable a temporary feature-flag to restore cross-subdomain session cookies for your tenant while we roll the fix.

Ava (support): Customer on call 16:00 PT, wants firm ETA. I'll coordinate the call and share your notes.

InfraBot: Action item created: #INC-4872 "AcmeApp embedded SSO cookie split / MFA loop" assigned to Liam, Samir. Priority: high.

Samir (eng): One more diagnostic ask — can AcmeApp provide a failing user agent + full set-cookie trace (Network tab -> copy as HAR)? That will help verify SameSite behavior across browsers. Chrome recently tightened SameSite rules which could also be amplifying the issue.

Ava (support): Will request HAR and include example user agent strings. Thanks all — keeping this thread updated during the patch. :thumbsup:
